mainTopic: Why רבי יהודה does not fear eating חדש before the עומר, and when חדש becomes permitted
overview: The amud opens by explaining why רבי יהודה is not afraid that someone handling new grain (חדש) before the עומר will eat it, even though he worries about this with חמץ. The first answer is that harvesting, grinding and sifting are done in unusual ways, which remind the person. A בית השלחין, where normal harvesting is allowed, knocks that answer down. אביי then says people keep away from חדש all year, but not from חמץ. רבא accepts this for רבי יהודה, and adds that the רבנן do not worry about חמץ because a person searching for it in order to burn it will not eat it. רב אשי suggests that only parched flour was prepared, but the גמרא rejects his answer as a mistake. A new משנה teaches that the עומר permits חדש, and that after the חורבן רבן יוחנן בן זכאי forbade the whole day, which רבי יהודה says is Torah law. In the גמרא, רב and שמואל say dawn permits חדש only when there is no בית המקדש. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש say dawn permits it always, and they read every source that ties the permission to the עומר as 'למצוה', the ideal way.

steps.title: Picking by hand reminds him not to eat
steps.stepSummary: Before the עומר, harvesting is allowed only by picking by hand. That unusual method keeps the person aware that the grain is still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since you allowed him to harvest only by picking by hand, he will remember.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer to the earlier question: why is there no fear that someone will eat new grain while handling it before the עומר?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that a person busy with grain might forget it is forbidden and eat some. Because he must harvest in a strange way (קיטוף, picking by hand), the strangeness itself reminds him. That is why no extra גזירה is needed here, unlike with חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Picking or plucking by hand, an unusual way to harvest
He remembers (that it is forbidden)
New grain, forbidden to eat until the עומר is brought
The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן that permits the new grain
A reminder or sign that keeps a person aware of an איסור

phrases.english: Since you did not permit it to him
phrases.notes: "It" is harvesting the new grain before the עומר.

phrases.english: except by means of picking by hand,
he remembers.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁלֹּא הִיתַּרְתָּה לוֹ אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי קִיטּוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised just before this section, comparing new grain to חמץ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing factor: the unusual method acts as a reminder
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think a person handling new grain would forget and eat it, just as רבי יהודה fears with חמץ
steps.terutzMaskana: Harvesting is allowed only by picking by hand, and that unusual method reminds him not to eat

steps.title: אביי asks about grinding and sifting
steps.stepSummary: אביי accepts the answer for harvesting, but says grinding and sifting seem to be done the normal way, so there is no reminder.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Fine for harvesting. But what can you say about grinding and sifting?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges the answer from Step 1. It works for harvesting, but not for the later stages of preparing the grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 1 depends on the work being done in an unusual way. Grinding and sifting appear to be done normally, so there should be no reminder at those stages, and the fear that he will eat should come back.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one case, but...)
Harvesting
Grinding
Sifting flour
What can be said? (a challenge)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
This works out well for harvesting,
but grinding and sifting,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח קְצִירָה, טְחִינָה וְהַרְקָדָה, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reminder answer of Step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that an unusual method reminds the person
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Grinding and sifting seem to be done normally, so there is no reminder at those stages

steps.title: Grinding and sifting are also done unusually
steps.stepSummary: Grinding is done with a small hand mill, and sifting is done on top of the sieve. Both are unusual, so the reminder is there too.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult: grinding is with a hand mill, and sifting is on top of the sieve.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי. Before the עומר, grinding and sifting are also done in an unusual way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from Step 1 now covers every stage. Grinding uses a hand mill instead of a big mill, and sifting happens on the back of the sieve instead of inside it. Each strange method keeps the person aware that the grain is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult (an answer is coming)
A hand mill
A sieve or sifter
On top of / on the back of

steps.whatToRemember: Before the עומר, every stage (harvesting, grinding, sifting) is done in an unusual way. That unusual way works as a reminder not to eat the new grain.

phrases.english: This is not difficult,
grinding is done with a hand mill,
sifting is done on top of the sieve.
phrases.notes: Normally you sift inside the sieve. Here it is done on its back side, which is unusual.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in Step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extends the same reasoning: the later stages are also done in an unusual way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Grinding and sifting are done in the normal way, so there is no reminder
steps.terutzMaskana: Grinding with a hand mill and sifting on top of the sieve are unusual, so the reminder still works

steps.title: Challenge from an irrigated field where normal harvesting is allowed
steps.stepSummary: In a בית השלחין, a regular harvest is allowed before the עומר, so there is no reminder. Why is there no fear here?
steps.simpleTranslation: An irrigated field, where harvesting is allowed, as we learned: One may harvest irrigated fields in the valleys, but one may not pile the grain. What can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge. There is a case where normal harvesting before the עומר is allowed, so the reminder answer seems to fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer so far relied on harvesting being allowed only by hand. But a משנה allows regular harvesting (קוצרין) in an irrigated field. In that case nothing unusual reminds the person, so why doesn't רבי יהודה worry that he will eat? The next step answers this with a completely new approach.

keyTerms.meaning: A field that needs watering (irrigation)
Valleys, where grain ripens early
Piling up the harvested grain into stacks
It is permitted

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two verbs. Harvesting (קוצרין) is allowed here in the normal way, but piling the grain (גודשין) is still forbidden.

phrases.english: An irrigated field, where harvesting is permitted,
as we learned in a משנה: One may harvest irrigated fields
phrases.notes: This is the משנה on מנחות 71a. The plain word "harvest" means a normal harvest, not picking by hand.

phrases.english: that are in the valleys, but one may not pile the grain.
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the answer in Step 3, raises a new case where the reminder reasoning seems to fail
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that harvesting before the עומר is always done by hand, which works as a reminder
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה allows normal harvesting in a בית השלחין, so there is no reminder, and the fear of eating should come back

steps.title: אביי's new answer: people stay away from חדש, but not from חמץ
steps.stepSummary: אביי drops the earlier answers about unusual methods. He says the real difference is that people naturally keep away from חדש, while they do not keep away from חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: from new grain, a person keeps his distance. From חמץ, a person does not keep his distance.
steps.whatsHappening: After the challenge about בית השלחין, אביי sets the 'reminder' approach aside. He gives a completely new reason why there is no fear with new grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חדש is forbidden all year until the עומר, so people are used to staying away from it and will not eat it by mistake. חמץ is allowed all year and eaten all the time, so a person handling it on פסח could easily slip and eat it. That is why רבי יהודה worries about חמץ but not about new grain.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: the earlier approach is set aside and a new one is offered
New grain, forbidden to eat until the עומר is brought
Leavened food, forbidden on פסח but allowed the rest of the year
Keeps away from it, separates himself from it
The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן that permits the new grain

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer moves the focus from how the grain is processed to the person's habits. Something forbidden all year is less likely to be eaten by mistake than something usually allowed.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
From new grain, one keeps his distance;
from chametz, one does not keep his distance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the בית השלחין challenge by replacing the whole reminder approach with a new reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New distinction based on the person's habits, not on the processing method
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lack of worry about new grain comes from unusual processing methods that remind the person.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lack of worry comes from the fact that people keep away from חדש all year, but not from חמץ.

steps.title: רבא: what about the contradiction in the רבנן's view?
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי: your answer only handles the contradiction in רבי יהודה. But the רבנן have a matching contradiction that your reasoning does not fix.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: is only רבי יהודה's ruling against רבי יהודה's ruling a problem, while the רבנן's ruling against the רבנן's ruling is not a problem?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא points out that the רבנן also seem to contradict themselves. They worry about new grain but not about חמץ. אביי's answer does not help them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By אביי's logic, חמץ should be the bigger worry, since people do not usually keep away from it. Yet the רבנן are the ones who do not worry about חמץ, while they are careful about new grain. So אביי's reasoning actually makes the רבנן's position look backwards.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty, a problem
The Sages, the majority opinion arguing with רבי יהודה

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate contradictions here: one inside רבי יהודה's views and one inside the רבנן's views. רבא wants an answer that handles both.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Is the contradiction of Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda difficult,
while that of the Rabbis against the Rabbis is not difficult?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קַשְׁיָא, דְּרַבָּנַן אַדְּרַבָּנַן לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's answer from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's distinction that people keep away from חדש but not from חמץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The distinction solves רבי יהודה's contradiction but leaves the רבנן's matching contradiction unanswered. In fact it makes it worse, since by that logic חמץ should be the bigger worry.

steps.title: רבא answers both contradictions
steps.stepSummary: רבא accepts אביי's answer for רבי יהודה: people keep away from חדש. For the רבנן, he explains that someone searching for חמץ in order to burn it will not eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: רבי יהודה against רבי יהודה is not a problem, as we already answered. The רבנן against the רבנן is also not a problem. The person himself is searching for the חמץ in order to burn it. Would he eat from it?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own full solution. רבי יהודה is answered by what was just said: people keep away from חדש. The רבנן are answered by looking at the person's purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, רבא keeps אביי's answer: people stay away from חדש all year, but not from חמץ. For the רבנן, a person hunting for חמץ is focused on destroying it, so there is no fear he will eat it. But someone processing new grain is getting it ready to eat, so there is real reason to worry.

keyTerms.meaning: As we answered before
Searches for it, goes looking for it
In order to burn it

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a person's goal while handling a forbidden item affects whether חז"ל worry he might eat it.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda is not difficult,
as we answered.
phrases.notes: He means אביי's answer just before: people keep away from חדש, but not from חמץ.

phrases.english: The Rabbis against the Rabbis is not difficult:
he himself is searching for it in order to burn it;
would he eat from it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers his own challenge from step 6. He keeps אביי's answer for רבי יהודה and adds a separate answer for the רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two separate answers: אביי's answer (keeping away from חדש) for רבי יהודה, and the person's purpose for the רבנן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי's distinction explains רבי יהודה, but the רבנן's view (worrying about חדש but not חמץ) seems to have no explanation.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה is answered by אביי's point that people keep away from חדש. The רבנן are answered because someone searching for חמץ in order to burn it will not eat it.

steps.title: רב אשי: before the עומר they made only flour of parched grain
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer for רבי יהודה. The new grain prepared before the עומר was made into flour of parched grain, which is not eaten as it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: רבי יהודה against רבי יהודה is not a problem. We learned in the משנה 'flour of parched grain'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers another way to solve רבי יהודה's contradiction. He points to the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the markets were full of 'flour of parched grain'. That kind of flour still needs more preparation before anyone eats it. So there is no fear that a person will eat it by mistake before the עומר, while חמץ is ready to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: Flour made from parched (roasted) grain
Parched, roasted grain

steps.whatToRemember: Three answers were offered for why רבי יהודה does not worry about new grain: unusual processing methods (רבה, knocked down by the בית השלחין case), people keep away from חדש (אביי, which רבא accepts), and the grain was only made into parched flour that is not eaten as it is (רב אשי).

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda is not difficult;
we learned 'flour of parched grain.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another answer to רבי יהודה's contradiction, different from אביי's answer that רבא accepted.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: New grain prepared before the עומר could be eaten right away, so there should be a fear that someone will eat it by mistake.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only flour of parched grain was prepared, which is not eaten as it is, so there is no fear of eating it by mistake.

steps.title: רב אשי's answer does not cover the grain before it became parched
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא calls רב אשי's answer a mistake. His idea works only after the grain became parched flour, not before.
steps.simpleTranslation: This answer of רב אשי is a mistake. It works from the time the grain became parched grain and on. But before it became parched grain, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב אשי's answer from Step 8. His answer does not cover the time before the grain was turned into parched flour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said there was no fear of eating the new grain because it had become קמח קלי, which people do not eat as it is. But the grain had to exist as normal, edible kernels first. During that earlier time the old question comes back: why are we not afraid someone will eat it?

keyTerms.meaning: A mistake; a statement that does not hold up
Parched (roasted) grain
It works out fine (for this part)

phrases.english: And this statement of רב אשי is a mistake,
it works out well from the parched-grain stage and onward,
but until it became parched grain, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks and rejects the answer רב אשי gave in Step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב אשי's whole answer for רבי יהודה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores the earlier stage, when the grain was still regular kernels that people could eat.

steps.title: Hand-picking cannot save רב אשי because of the irrigated field
steps.stepSummary: Someone might defend רב אשי by saying the grain was picked by hand, like רבה said. But that brings back the problem of the בית השלחין, where regular harvesting is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that here too it was picked by hand, like רבה said, what will you say about an irrigated field, where regular harvesting is allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way to rescue רב אשי, using רבה's idea of hand-picking as the reminder for the earlier stage. Then it knocks that rescue down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rescue says that before the grain was parched, the unusual hand-picking reminded people not to eat it. But we already saw in Step 4 that this idea fails. In a בית השלחין a regular harvest is allowed before the עומר, so there is no reminder at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Picking grain by hand instead of cutting it with a sickle
An irrigated field, which may be harvested before the עומר
Harvesting in the normal way
And if you would say (bringing a possible defense)

phrases.english: And if you would say that here too
it was done by picking by hand, like רבה said,
then about an irrigated field, where harvesting is permitted,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: וכי תימא הכא נמי על ידי קיטוף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to fix the gap found in Step 9, then shows that the fix fails.
steps.kashyaTarget: The defense of רב אשי that uses רבה's hand-picking idea
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Hand-picking cannot be the reminder, because in a בית השלחין normal harvesting is allowed before the עומר.

steps.title: Final verdict: רב אשי's answer is rejected
steps.stepSummary: Since no defense works, the גמרא concludes that רב אשי's answer is a mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this statement of רב אשי is a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion by repeating that רב אשי's answer does not stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repetition is the final ruling after the rescue in Step 10 failed. The answers that remain are אביי's idea that people keep away from חדש, and רבא's answers.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introducing the final position)

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי's parched-flour answer is rejected. The grain had an edible stage before it was parched, and hand-picking cannot cover that stage because of the בית השלחין.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, הָא דְּרַב אָשֵׁי בְּרוּתָא הִיא.
phrases.english: Rather, this statement of רב אשי is a mistake.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא הא דרב אשי ברותא היא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final verdict after the defense in Step 10 failed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב אשי's answer is rejected as a mistake.

steps.title: חדש is permitted once the עומר is offered
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: when the עומר is offered, חדש becomes permitted right away. People far from ירושלים may eat it from midday on.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the עומר is offered, the new grain is permitted immediately. People who live far away are permitted from midday and onward.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches when חדש becomes permitted in the time of the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The offering of the עומר is what permits the new grain. People far away cannot know exactly when it was offered, so they wait until midday. By then it has surely been brought.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן
Grain from the new crop, forbidden until the עומר
Those who live far from the בית המקדש
Midday

phrases.english: Mishnah
Once the עומר was offered,
new grain was permitted immediately;
those far away are permitted
from midday and onward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offering the עומר permits חדש right away. People far away may eat it from midday.

steps.title: After the חורבן the whole day is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: After the חורבן, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made a rule that the whole day of waving is forbidden for חדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the בית המקדש was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made a rule that the whole day of waving is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the rule after the חורבן. With no עומר being brought, חדש is forbidden for the entire 16th of ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the בית המקדש stood, the offering itself permitted the grain during the day. Without it, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made people wait the whole day. The משנה calls this a תקנה, an enactment.

keyTerms.meaning: The day the עומר was waved, the 16th of ניסן
Made a rule (enacted a תקנה)
Once the Temple was destroyed

phrases.english: Once the Temple was destroyed,
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai enacted
that the entire day of waving should be forbidden.
phrases.notes: So nowadays new grain may be eaten only starting the next day.

steps.triggerLanguage: משחרב בית המקדש התקין רבן יוחנן בן זכאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the rule for after the חורבן to the rule for Temple times in Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the חורבן, the whole יום הנף is forbidden for חדש.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: it is Torah law, and why the far-away people could eat at midday
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the whole day is forbidden by the Torah itself, not by an enactment. People far away could eat from midday because they trusted the court to bring the עומר early.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: Isn't it forbidden by the Torah? It says "until this very day." So why could people far away eat from midday? Because they know the court is not lazy about bringing it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues with how the משנה described רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's rule. He also explains the midday rule for people far away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads "עד עצם היום הזה" as forbidding the whole day when there is no offering. So רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was teaching a Torah law, not making a new rule. In Temple times, people far away relied on the בית דין bringing the עומר quickly, so by midday it had surely been offered.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law, not a rabbinic rule
"Until this very day" (ויקרא 23:14)
Being lazy or slow
The court in charge of bringing the עומר

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה agrees that the whole day is forbidden today. He disagrees only about why: he holds it is Torah law, not an enactment of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא will need to work out what רבי יהודה means by calling the ban Torah law, since the משנה called it an enactment.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
But isn't it forbidden by Torah law,
as it says, "until this very day"?
So for what reason are those far away permitted
from midday and onward?
Because they know
that the court is not lazy about it.
phrases.notes: He means the court brings the עומר early, so by midday it has surely been offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי יהודה והלא מן התורה הוא אסור
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with the משנה's description in Step 13 of the rule as an enactment, and explains the midday rule from Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without an offering, the whole day is forbidden by Torah law. People far away ate from midday only because they trusted the court to bring the עומר quickly.

steps.title: רב and שמואל: the עומר permits when the בית המקדש stands, dawn permits when it does not
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל say that the עומר permits חדש while the בית המקדש stands. When there is no בית המקדש, the dawn of the day permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב and שמואל both say: When the בית המקדש is standing, the עומר permits the new grain. When the בית המקדש is not standing, the light of dawn in the east permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion with a ruling from רב and שמואל. They say what makes חדש permitted, both when there is a בית המקדש and when there is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה in the משנה said the whole day stays forbidden after the חורבן. רב and שמואל disagree: without a בית המקדש, חדש becomes permitted as soon as dawn breaks on that day. With a בית המקדש, you must wait until the עומר is actually brought.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the sixteenth of ניסן that permits the new grain
Permits, makes something allowed
The eastern sky lit up, meaning dawn
At a time when the בית המקדש is standing
Both of them

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main disagreement of the section: does dawn alone ever permit חדש when the בית המקדש is standing?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav and Shmuel both say:
When the Temple is standing,
the omer permits the new grain.
When the Temple is not standing,
the lighting up of the east permits it.
phrases.notes: This means dawn on the sixteenth of ניסן, the day the עומר would have been brought.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה, giving a view different from רבי יהודה's about the time after the חורבן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a בית המקדש, the עומר permits חדש. Without a בית המקדש, dawn of the sixteenth permits it.

steps.title: What is the source? Two phrases seem to give different times
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רב and שמואל's reason. It points out that the פסוק gives two endpoints: 'until the day you bring' and 'until this very day.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Two verses are written. It says 'until the day you bring the offering,' and it also says 'until this very day.' How can both be true?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רב and שמואל get their rule. It shows two phrases that seem to clash, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One phrase ties the permission to bringing the עומר. The other ties it to the day itself, which would mean dawn. 'הא כיצד' asks how the two can fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Two verses (here, two phrases in the same פסוק)
Until the day you bring (the offering)
Until this very day
How can this be? How do these fit together?

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Two verses are written:
phrases.notes: Both phrases actually come from one פסוק, ויקרא 23:14.

phrases.english: It is written: 'until the day you bring',
and it is written: 'until this very day.'
How can this be?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רב and שמואל's two-part rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for having two different times of permission, and how the two phrases fit together.

steps.title: One phrase for when the בית המקדש stands, one for when it does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'until you bring' applies when the בית המקדש stands, and 'until this very day' applies when it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, it is talking about when the בית המקדש is standing. There, it is talking about when the בית המקדש is not standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by giving each phrase its own time period. This is exactly the rule of רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Until you bring the offering' only makes sense when there is a בית המקדש to bring it in. 'Until this very day' covers the time with no בית המקדש, when the day itself, from dawn, permits חדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there; one case versus the other
When the בית המקדש is not standing

steps.confusionAlert: The text says only 'here' and 'here' without naming the phrases. The first 'here' (בית המקדש standing) matches 'until you bring.' The second (no בית המקדש) matches 'until this very day.'

phrases.english: Here, when the Temple is standing;
phrases.notes: This 'here' is the phrase 'until the day you bring.'

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן – בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים.
phrases.english: there, when the Temple is not standing.
phrases.notes: This one is the phrase 'until this very day.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by assigning each phrase to a different time period.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Until you bring' applies when the בית המקדש stands. 'Until this very day' applies when it does not.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב and שמואל, both phrases of the פסוק are needed. Each one covers a different time period.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש: dawn permits even when the בית המקדש stands
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש say that dawn permits חדש even while the בית המקדש is standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both say: Even when the בית המקדש is standing, the light of dawn in the east permits the new grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion that disagrees with רב and שמואל. Here dawn permits חדש at all times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and שמואל needed the עומר itself while there is a בית המקדש. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש say that by Torah law it is the day that permits, even when there is a בית המקדש. This sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Even

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish both say:
Even when the Temple is standing,
the lighting up of the east permits it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a view that disagrees with רב and שמואל about the time when the בית המקדש stands.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dawn of the sixteenth permits חדש, even when the בית המקדש is standing.

steps.title: But the verse says 'until you bring'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש from the phrase 'until you bring,' which seems to require the עומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'until you bring'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the opinion of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש using the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'until you bring' seems to say חדש stays forbidden until the עומר is actually brought. If dawn alone permits, what is this phrase for?

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: But isn't it written: 'until you bring'!
phrases.notes: This is the same phrase from ויקרא 23:14 quoted earlier, just in short form.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the opinion just stated.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש's rule that dawn permits even while the בית המקדש stands.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק ties the permission to bringing the עומר, which seems to rule out dawn as the time of permission when there is a בית המקדש.

steps.title: Waiting for the עומר is only the ideal way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'until you bring' is למצוה: the best way is to wait for the עומר, but by law חדש is already permitted at dawn.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is for the מצוה: the ideal way is to wait, but it is permitted from dawn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. It explains that the phrase only teaches the best way to act, not what is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed 'until you bring' sets a strict prohibition. The answer reads it as a recommendation: the right way is to wait for the עומר, but if someone eats after dawn, he has not eaten something forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: For the מצוה; the ideal way, not a strict requirement
From the start, the preferred way of doing something

phrases.english: It is for the מצוה.
phrases.notes: He means it is best to wait for the עומר, but the grain is already allowed from dawn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the force of the פסוק, from a strict requirement to the ideal way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Until you bring' means חדש is forbidden until the עומר is brought.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Until you bring' is only the ideal way. By law, dawn already permits חדש.
steps.whatToRemember: רב and שמואל: with a בית המקדש, the עומר permits; without one, dawn permits. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש: dawn always permits, and waiting for the עומר is only למצוה.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה: new grain is permitted right after the עומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש from the משנה, which says חדש was permitted immediately once the עומר was offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: once the עומר was offered, new grain was permitted right away! That sounds like the עומר is what permits it, not dawn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes our משנה to challenge רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש again. The משנה links the permission of חדש to the offering of the עומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If dawn already permitted חדש, the עומר would not be what makes it allowed. Yet the משנה says 'once the עומר was offered, חדש was permitted immediately.' This makes it sound like before the עומר, חדש was still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן
New grain of this year's crop, forbidden until the עומר
Immediately, right away

phrases.english: From when the עומר was offered,
the new grain was permitted immediately!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to the same view, this time from the משנה instead of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש's view that dawn permits חדש even when the בית המקדש stands
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes the permission depend on the offering of the עומר, which implies חדש is still forbidden before it.

steps.title: Answer: the משנה describes the best way, not the strict law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה means 'למצוה': ideally one waits for the עומר, but by law dawn already permits חדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is only for the מצוה, the best way to act.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer it gave to the פסוק in Step 20. The משנה is describing the ideal practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is not saying חדש is forbidden until the עומר. It is saying the best way to fulfill the מצוה is to wait until the עומר is offered. Strictly, dawn already permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: For the מצוה: the ideal way, not the strict requirement
The finest, most ideal way to do a מצוה
Dawn, when the eastern sky lights up

phrases.english: For the מצוה.
phrases.notes: Meaning: waiting for the עומר is the best way, but you are not strictly required to wait.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21 using the same idea as Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source as describing the ideal practice rather than the strict law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה means חדש is forbidden until the עומר is offered.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means it is best to wait for the עומר, but by law חדש is permitted from dawn.

steps.title: Challenge from the next משנה: the עומר permits outside the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again from another משנה, which says the עומר is what permits new grain in the country.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: the עומר would permit new grain in the rest of the country, and the שתי הלחם permitted it in the בית המקדש! Again, the עומר seems to be what permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third source against רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. This משנה calls the עומר the thing that 'permits' new grain outside the Temple.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מתיר' (permits) suggests the עומר itself removes the איסור. If dawn already did that, why call the עומר the thing that permits? This seems to clash with רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Permits; makes something allowed
The country, everywhere outside the בית המקדש
The two loaves offering brought on שבועות
The Temple

phrases.english: The עומר would permit in the country,
phrases.notes: This is the next משנה. 'The country' means everywhere outside the Temple.

phrases.english: and the two loaves in the Temple!
phrases.notes: The two loaves let new grain be used for offerings in the Temple itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another challenge to the same view, from a different משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש's view that dawn permits חדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה calls the עומר the thing that 'permits' new grain in the country, implying it is forbidden before the עומר.

steps.title: Same answer: the עומר is only the ideal time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers again 'למצוה': waiting for the עומר is the best practice, while by law dawn already permits חדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: That too is only for the מצוה, the best way to act.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers this third challenge exactly like the first two. The view of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the משנה says the עומר 'permits' new grain, it means that is the ideal time to start eating it. It does not mean the grain is truly forbidden before that. So all three sources (the פסוק and both משניות) fit with 'dawn permits by law.'

keyTerms.meaning: Ideally, from the start
By strict law
Permission; being allowed

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, dawn of the 16th of ניסן permits חדש by law even when the בית המקדש stands. Every source that links it to the עומר is read as 'למצוה', the ideal way.
steps.confusionAlert: 'למצוה' does not mean eating חדש before the עומר is forbidden. It means waiting is the better way, but eating after dawn is allowed by law.

phrases.english: For the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23 with the same 'למצוה' idea used in Steps 20 and 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source as describing the ideal practice rather than the strict law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה means the עומר is what removes the איסור of חדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עומר is only the ideal time to begin eating חדש. By law it is already permitted from dawn.
